title: Siang dam protesters released in Arunachal Pradesh after nearly a month in detention

ai.summary: Four protesters detained over the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh were released after nearly a month in jail, following the state government's goodwill gesture to address demands from the Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum.

facts.claim: Four protesters detained over the proposed 11,220-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh were released from Jully Central Jail near Itanagar on Saturday (November 7, 2026), nearly a month after their arrest
facts.quote: Four protesters detained over the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh were released from Jully Central Jail near Itanagar on Saturday (November 7, 2026), nearly a month after their arrest, officials said.

facts.claim: The four, identified as Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron, were detained on October 9 under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014
facts.quote: The four, identified as Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron, were detained on October 9 under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014, they added.

facts.claim: Their release came a day after the State Government agreed to free them as a goodwill gesture while responding to demands raised by the Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum (SIFF), which has been leading the protest against the proposed mega dam
facts.quote: Their release came a day after the State Government agreed to free them as a goodwill gesture while responding to demands raised by the Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum (SIFF), which has been leading the protest against the proposed mega dam.

facts.claim: The development marks a significant step towards easing tensions in the Siang Valley, where opposition to the project has triggered protests and confrontations in recent months
facts.quote: The development marks a significant step towards easing tensions in the Siang Valley, where opposition to the project has triggered protests and confrontations in recent months.

facts.claim: The Government, however, maintained that the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters would have to follow due legal process
facts.quote: The Government, however, maintained that the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters would have to follow due legal process.

facts.claim: The Government has urged SIFF to resume dialogue and communicate a convenient date, along with a list of delegates, for a proposed meeting with Chief Minister Pema Khandu
facts.quote: The Government has urged SIFF to resume dialogue and communicate a convenient date, along with a list of delegates, for a proposed meeting with Chief Minister Pema Khandu.

ai.background_note: The Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum (SIFF) has been leading protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh, citing concerns about displacement, submergence of ancestral villages, and environmental impacts.
